heroHeadline: UN Report Ties UAE, Colombia and Ethiopia to RSF War Machine as Blue Nile Fighting Displaces Nearly 20,000
heroSubtitle: A UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission reported on September 3, 2026 that a transnational network spanning the UAE, Colombia, Chad, Libya, and Somalia has supplied the RSF with weapons, training, and roughly 2,000 foreign contractors operating combat drones, urging the Security Council to expand Sudan's arms embargo nationwide. The report landed the same day Sovereignty Council chief Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan visited Ed Damazin to inspect the army's 4th Infantry Division amid an RSF-SPLM-N buildup near the Ethiopian border, and a Kurmuk-area commissioner separately accused Ethiopia of hosting four UAE-backed RSF training camps — a claim Sudan Tribune said it could not independently verify. The diplomatic flurry follows a week of escalation in Blue Nile: RSF and allied SPLM-N (al-Hilu) fighters claimed capture of the army's Bakori and Sirkam bases southeast of Damazin on August 28, displacing nearly 20,000 people within two days even as the army rushed in an elite reinforcement brigade and roughly 200 more RSF fighters — led by a North Kordofan intelligence chief — defected to the army in Omdurman on August 31. SAF Chief of Staff Yasir al-Atta vowed on September 1 that neither the UN Security Council nor the UAE could halt the army's advances, promising a multi-pronged offensive. Separately, WFP confirmed an unattributed aerial attack destroyed two food trucks bound for famine-hit Kadugli outside Dilling, South Kordofan on August 30. Day 1239 of the SAF-RSF war with no ceasefire and famine conditions persisting across Darfur and Kordofan.
